title: Cost to Paint a House in Richmond, TX (2026)
description: How much does it cost to paint a house in Richmond, TX? Exterior repaints run $2,500–$16,000+, interiors $3,000–$20,000+, cabinets from $650. Free estimate.
author: Chris Petkau

content:
The cost to paint a house in Richmond, TX depends almost entirely on what you’re painting. A whole-home exterior repaint typically runs $2,500 to $16,000+, a full interior lands between $3,000 and $20,000+, and kitchen cabinets start at a $650 minimum and run up to $7,500+ for a large kitchen with an island. The exact figure comes down to your home’s size, its age, the surfaces involved, and how much prep the job really needs.

I’m Chris, owner of The Proud Paintbrush. We’ve painted homes all over Richmond — from newer builds in Aliana, Harvest Green, and Veranda to established homes in Long Meadow Farms and Pecan Grove, plus the older character homes around the Old Richmond historic district. Richmond is unusual because the housing stock is so mixed, and that mix is exactly what drives the price. Here’s the honest breakdown.

What drives the cost to paint a Richmond home?

Richmond spans two very different worlds. On one side you have master-planned communities like Aliana, Harvest Green, and Veranda, where homes are newer, often two stories, and clad in a brick-and-HardiePlank mix. On the other you have Pecan Grove, Long Meadow Farms, and the Old Richmond historic district, where homes are older, sometimes wood-sided, and carry more years of sun and weather. Both can be beautiful repaints — they just price differently.

The main cost drivers are the same ones that matter on any Fort Bend home:

  • Size and stories. Square footage and wall area do most of the work. A single-story home in Pecan Grove is a very different job than a 3,500-square-foot two-story in Aliana, where the second story adds ladder and scaffold time, more equipment, and more labor hours.
  • Older vs. newer stock. Newer Harvest Green and Veranda homes usually have sound surfaces and need less prep. Older Pecan Grove and historic-district homes often carry weathered wood, failed caulk, and chalking paint — all of which add prep labor before any color goes on.
  • Surface type. Wood siding, fiber-cement (HardiePlank), brick, and stucco each prep and coat differently. Wood needs careful scraping and protection, fiber-cement has miles of board edges to cut in by hand, brick wants a breathable coating, and stucco soaks up more paint.
  • Condition and prep. This is the single biggest variable. Pressure washing, scraping, caulking, wood repair, and priming all happen before the finish coat. A sound exterior is straightforward; one with peeling paint or rotted trim carries real prep cost.

Exterior painting cost in Richmond

Most Richmond exterior repaints fall between $2,500 and $16,000+, and the typical whole-home repaint lands between $4,500 and $15,000+ depending on siding, height, and prep. Here’s where most homes land:

  • Small homes & partial exteriors: $2,500–$5,000
  • Medium homes: $5,000–$10,000
  • Large homes & full two-story repaints: $10,000–$16,000+

Our exterior rates run about $2.00–$2.50 per square foot on walls, $1.75–$2.50 per linear foot on trim, $120–$180 per door, and $250–$600 per garage door. You can see the full breakdown on our exterior painting price ranges page. The older homes around Old Richmond deserve a special note: historic-district and aged-wood exteriors almost always need more scraping, spot-priming, and wood repair, which pushes them toward the higher end of their size band even when the home isn’t large. That prep isn’t an upsell — it’s what makes a coating actually last on weathered wood in the Gulf Coast climate.

Interior painting cost in Richmond

Inside, most homeowners invest between $3,000 and $20,000+ for a full interior, with smaller projects priced by scope:

  • Single room: $500–$1,500
  • Multiple rooms: $1,500–$5,000
  • Full interior: $3,000–$20,000+

Our interior rates are $2.00 per square foot on walls, $1.20 per square foot on ceilings, $1.92 per linear foot on baseboards, $96 per door, and $54 per window, with primer at $1.00 per square foot when it’s needed for new drywall, stain blocking, or a dark-to-light color change. The two-story foyers and vaulted great rooms common in Aliana and Veranda add access cost — high ceilings mean more setup and labor — while a furnished, occupied home also takes longer than an empty one. Full pricing is on our Richmond interior painting page.

Cabinet painting cost in Richmond

Kitchen cabinet painting is its own category because it’s the most detail-intensive work we do. Pricing is built per door ($120–$145) and per drawer ($110–$135), with a $650 job minimum:

  • Bathroom vanity: $650–$1,200
  • Typical kitchen (about 25 doors, 10 drawers): $4,100–$5,000
  • Large kitchen with island & built-ins: $5,500–$7,500+

That price reflects real work: removing and labeling doors and hardware, degreasing, sanding, priming for adhesion, and a controlled spray finish that cures to a smooth, factory-like result. It’s why a quality cabinet job outlasts a quick brush-and-roll — see our Richmond cabinet painting page for the full process and ranges.

What a quality Richmond quote includes

When you compare estimates, the number only means something if you know what’s behind it. A complete quote should spell out the prep — pressure washing, scraping, caulking, wood repair, and priming — not just the paint. When one bid comes in far below the rest, it’s almost never a discount; it’s usually a spray-and-go that skips the prep, and those shortcuts show up a year or two later as peeling seams and uneven fade. Redoing a rushed job costs you twice, because the next crew has to repair the failure before they can even start.

No phone-quote guesswork, no skipped steps.

How to get an exact figure for your home

Every Richmond home is different, so the only accurate price is one based on your actual walls, trim, and surfaces. We walk the property in person, check the condition and siding type, talk through colors and prep, and hand you a clear written number — with no pressure. Whether you’re repainting a newer two-story in Harvest Green or freshening up an older home near Old Richmond, that walkthrough is what pins your project down inside the ranges above.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much does it cost to paint a house exterior in Richmond, TX?

Most Richmond exterior repaints run $2,500 to $16,000+, with the typical whole-home repaint between $4,500 and $15,000+. The exact figure depends on size, number of stories, siding type, and how much prep the home needs.

Do older Richmond homes cost more to paint?

Often, yes. Older homes in Pecan Grove and the Old Richmond historic district frequently have weathered wood, failed caulk, and chalking paint, which add scraping, priming, and wood-repair labor before the finish coat — pushing them toward the higher end of their size band.

How much does it cost to paint kitchen cabinets in Richmond?

A typical kitchen (about 25 doors and 10 drawers) runs $4,100–$5,000, and a large kitchen with an island or built-ins runs $5,500–$7,500+. Pricing is built per door ($120–$145) and per drawer ($110–$135), with a $650 minimum. A bathroom vanity runs $650–$1,200.

How much does interior painting cost in Richmond?

A single room runs $500–$1,500, multiple rooms $1,500–$5,000, and a full interior $3,000–$20,000+, depending on wall condition, ceiling height, trim detail, and number of colors.
